summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) has heated up again after a tense pause: UKMTO reported tankers attacked north of Oman's Khasab on Nov 17 and Nov 20, and a US military official told Reuters that US aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17. On Saturday, Nov 21, UKMTO reported two tanker incidents near Khasab (a projectile hit on one tanker's stern and another in a tanker's engine room, possibly the same vessel), and Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of the strait. Bahrain said two people were injured in an Iranian strike on a civilian industrial site on Nov 21, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US bases there. Iran's deputy foreign minister said a Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Nov 20 (AFP, Iran International). On Nov 22 the tracking firm TankerTrackers said ship-tracking signals showing an Iranian tanker, the Khat-Shekan, sailing through the strait toward the US blockade were a spoof and that the vessel does not exist (Euronews). On Sunday evening UKMTO reported a tanker incident involving military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, with investigations ongoing (Euronews). Iran's foreign minister said talks must be given a chance; no agreement has been announced. On Thursday, Nov 26, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more tankers hit sea mines north of Khasab, and UKMTO reported an explosion from an unknown projectile near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai (Reuters). Kuwait's Defense Ministry said two Italian technicians died after a drone attack on a site in Kuwait on Nov 26 and blamed Iran, which denied it (ABC News). On Friday, Nov 27, Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said a tanker exploded after hitting a mine north of Ghavam Island while another turned back; the ships were not named and the claim was not independently confirmed (Anadolu).

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera). This is the latest weekly figure found; no newer one had been confirmed by Nov 18.

status.label: The war
status.note: A US military official told Reuters that US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17, after earlier limited US strikes there on Nov 2 and Nov 7 and on launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik over Nov 15-16 (Euronews). On Nov 17 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US radar system in Bahrain with drones; Bahrain said it intercepted the attacks. Qatar, a mediator, called for restraint; no deal has been signed. On Nov 21 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they struck US bases in Bahrain; Bahrain said an Iranian strike on a civilian industrial site injured two people (AFP). A Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Nov 20, Iran's deputy foreign minister said (AFP).

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent settled at US$91.40 a barrel on Tuesday, Nov 24, up 2.27%, and US crude at US$82.05, up 2.35%, rebounding after touching three-month lows (US$88.10 and US$79.07) earlier in the day, on reports of attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz (The Nation; Forbes Middle East).

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said two oil tankers tried to pass through an unauthorised route north of Ghavam Island on Friday morning, Nov 27; it said one exploded after hitting a naval mine and the other turned back. It did not name the ships (Fars, via Anadolu).
sources: Anews (Anadolu): Iran says oil tanker explodes after hitting naval mine in Strait of Hormuz

updates.text: President Donald Trump said the US has "victory at hand" and is giving Tehran a chance to negotiate a deal (Al Jazeera).

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi called the deadly Nov 26 attack in Kuwait "suspicious" and said it looked like a "pre-cooked recipe for war"; Kuwait said two Italians died from falling debris as Iranian drones were intercepted (Al Jazeera).
sources: Al Jazeera live: Iran's Araghchi calls deadly Kuwait attack 'suspicious'

updates.text: Kuwait's Defense Ministry said two Italian technicians injured in a drone attack on a site in Kuwait on Nov 26 had died, and blamed Iran; Iran's armed forces spokesman denied any Iranian operation in the region (ABC News, IRNA via ABC; Italy's foreign minister named the men's employer, per HNGN).

Reuters reported on Nov 26 that UKMTO, citing local authorities, said an unidentified projectile struck a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz 18 nautical miles east of Oman's Khasab on Wednesday, Nov 25; all crew were accounted for and no environmental impact was reported.
sources: BOE Report (Reuters): Tanker struck by projectile while transiting Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says

updates.text: UKMTO reported on Nov 26 an explosion from an unknown projectile near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai (Reuters).
sources: Reuters via KWSN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit sea mines near Oman's Khasab

updates.text: Reuters reported on Nov 26 that Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers, one of them a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude, exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines north of Oman's Khasab while using an 'unauthorised' route; no independent confirmation of the mine strikes had been reported.
sources: Reuters via KWSN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit sea mines near Oman's Khasab
ABC News: Iran live updates: IRGC claims 2 oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz

updates.text: Al Arabiya and Arab News reported on Nov 25 that Iran's army said another oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, the third such report from Iran; no independent confirmation had been reported.
sources: Al Arabiya: Iran's army says oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
Arab News: Third tanker hits mine in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
